review.intro: Morning update. Each item opens the exact cut in the Cuts view (use the panels M_z / E/N / <A_v>,<B_p>; filled markers = up branch, hollow = dn branch). 'Stuck anchor' = a y-polarized starting state that missed the plaquette correlations (<B_p> ~0.05 instead of ~0.2), so its energy is ~5 too high.

items.title: 1. z<->y at h_x = 0, h_y = 1.5 — clean first-order jump
items.text: M_z jumps at h_z ~ 0.375 with a hysteresis loop (~0.25-0.5): the up branch rises steeply between 0.40 and 0.50, the dn branch drops between 0.35 and 0.25.

items.title: 2. z<->y at h_x = 0, h_y = 1.4 — up branch is being re-run
items.text: The old up branch started from a stuck anchor. It was replaced by the round-trip state (the dn branch continued down to h_z = 0.05, <B_p> 0.123 = good). Until the re-run chain lands (job 58806874, queued) only 1 up point is shown, so the locator temporarily reads 0.175 (the dn branch's drop). Before the reset it was 0.325.

items.title: 3. z<->y at h_x = 0, h_y = 1.6 — loop narrowing
items.text: Jump ~0.475; the up/dn gap is smaller than at 1.4-1.5.

items.title: 4. z<->y at h_x = 0, h_y = 1.7 — marginal
items.text: M_z rises steeply around 0.5 but the up/dn gap is small; locator 0.525, not flagged 'ok'.

items.title: 5. z<->y at h_x = 0, h_y = 1.8 — crossover (line has ended)
items.text: Both branches follow one M_z curve. They differ only in energy, which is the stuck-anchor effect, not hysteresis. So the z<->y line ends between h_y 1.7 and 1.8 (L = 4).

items.title: 6. z<->y at h_x = 0.2, h_y = 1.4 — jump shifted up by 0.05
items.text: Jump 0.375 (h_x = 0: 0.325). Loop ~0.20-0.45: up jumps between 0.40 and 0.45, dn drops between 0.25 and 0.20. The up anchor (h_z = 0.05) is stuck; left running as you asked.

items.title: 7. z<->y at h_x = 0.2, h_y = 1.5 — also +0.05
items.text: Jump 0.425 (h_x = 0: 0.375). Loop ~0.30-0.45. Up anchor stuck (left running).

items.title: 8. z<->y at h_x = 0.5, h_y = 1.4 — up branch only so far
items.text: M_z rises around h_z 0.45-0.5, i.e. about +0.15 vs h_x = 0 (your estimate). Not a confirmed jump yet: the dn branch is running now. h_x = 0.5 at h_y = 1.5 has no points yet.

items.title: 9. x<->y at h_z = 0, h_y = 1.3 — crossover (your in-plane-sweep test)
items.text: No jump and no hysteresis: up and dn agree to |dM_x| ~0.01 from h_x 0.75 to 1.25 and M_x rises smoothly. The x<->y line therefore ends between the pocket tip (h_y ~1.19) and 1.3.

items.title: 10. x<->y at h_z = 0, h_y = 1.4 — same picture so far
items.text: Up branch complete and smooth; the dn branch has 3 points so far.

items.title: 11. h_x = 0.2 roof, h_z = 0.15 — probably biased high
items.text: h_x = 0.2 roof: 1.185 / 1.175 / 1.225 / 1.225 at h_z = 0 / 0.1 / 0.15 / 0.2. This cut's dn anchor is stuck, so its 1.225 is likely too high (the same pattern as the h_x = 0 'tip').

items.title: 12. h_x = 0.2 roof, h_z = 0.2 — good anchor, still 1.225
items.text: Here the dn anchor is good and the roof still reads 1.225, so part of the rise toward h_z ~0.2 may be real.

items.title: 13. The h_x = 0 'tip' (h_z = 0.15) — anchor test pending
items.text: Roof 1.245 with a stuck dn anchor. Four recipe trials (continue / long / anneal from h_y = 3 / round trip) are still queued.

items.text: Phase diagram -> '(h_y, h_z) planes at fixed h_x'.
